title: Income-tax Act, 2025 — Structure, Commencement and Transition from the 1961 Act

content.overview: The Income-tax Act, 2025 is the restated income-tax code noted in this subject, with a commencement and a transition from the Income-tax Act, 1961. Topics in this subject that cite numbered 1961 sections state the 1961 rule. They are not to be renumbered into the 2025 Act unless the transition provision says the old section continues. Pending proceedings and returns for pre-commencement years follow the transition. The 2025 Act does not silently rewrite a 1961 section number in an older topic. The commencement and saving provisions control.

sections.body:
the assessee and Revenue bear burdens according to the charging provision, exemption or deduction claimed, assessment record, statutory presumption and appellate issue

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Forum and Limitation Checkpoints
sections.body:
Competent forum: the assessing authority, appellate authority, ITAT, GST appellate forum, High Court on a substantial question or constitutional writ jurisdiction, and Supreme Court according to the statute.
Check limitation, notice, alternative remedy, jurisdiction and statutory appeal or review route.
Transition and current law: identify the tax period, charging statute, commencement date, amendment or notification in force, taxable event, jurisdictional notice and statutory appeal or writ route; use the Income-tax Act, 1961 only as historical transition/concordance where the 2025 Act applies

cases.name: Govind Saran Ganga Saran v. Commissioner of Sales Tax
cases.facts: The Court examined the components of a valid charging provision.
cases.issue: What must a tax levy clearly identify to be valid?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A valid levy ordinarily identifies the taxable event, person liable, rate and measure or value of the tax.
cases.holding: The Court treated these components as essential to a charging scheme.
cases.relevance: Use for charge, levy and statutory certainty.

cases.name: Union of India v. Azadi Bachao Andolan
cases.facts: The Court considered treaty benefits, circulars and tax avoidance arguments.
cases.issue: How should a valid tax treaty and administrative circular operate?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A treaty and valid administrative practice must be respected unless displaced by law; legitimate tax planning is not automatically evasion.
cases.holding: The Court upheld the challenged treaty approach in the circumstances.
cases.relevance: Use for statutory interpretation, treaties and tax planning.

cases.name: Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt. Ltd.
cases.facts: The case concerned GST levy and the legal effect of a Council recommendation.
cases.issue: What is the constitutional and statutory force of GST Council recommendations?
cases.ratioDecidendi: GST Council recommendations have persuasive value within the constitutional design but are not automatically binding as primary legislation without statutory implementation.
cases.holding: The Court interpreted the federal GST framework accordingly.
cases.relevance: Use for GST levy, delegated action and constitutional federalism.

I. ISSUE AND JURISDICTION
Whether Income-tax Act, 2025 — Structure, Commencement and Transition from the 1961 Act applies to the stated facts and whether the chosen forum and remedy are maintainable.

II. GOVERNING RULE
Income-tax Act, 2025 — Structure, Commencement and Transition from the 1961 Act is governed by Income-tax Act, 2025; Income-tax Rules, 2026; CGST Act, 2017; IGST Act, 2017; applicable SGST Acts; and Customs Act, 1962, together with current rules, notifications and circulars. identify the tax period, charging statute, commencement date, amendment or notification in force, taxable event, jurisdictional notice and statutory appeal or writ route; use the Income-tax Act, 1961 only as historical transition/concordance where the 2025 Act applies.

III. INGREDIENT APPLICATION
Identify each condition, connect it to the evidence and answer the principal exception or defence. Apply BSA s. 63 to digital records where relevant and state the initial burden precisely.

IV. CONCLUSION
Grant, refuse or modify the relief only to the extent authorised by the governing law and proved record.

essentialIngredients: 1961 section used only for a pre-commencement year
enhancement.detailedExplanation: This topic is the transition marker. It records that a new Act was enacted to replace the 1961 Act from its commencement, and that assessment years before that commencement remain on the old Act. Section numbers in the other income-tax topics are 1961 numbers. A user of a post-commencement year must read the 2025 Act and the savings, not assume the old number survived. Rates remain in the Finance Act.
examples: A previous year before commencement is assessed under the 1961 Act.
A previous year after commencement is read under the 2025 Act and its savings.
A 1961 section number is not cited as the 2025 number.
